title: The Official Letter
intro: A letter arrives by post from a court. After today, any official letter feels like a trap.
But some messages are real. Mirage loves it when you stop trusting the honest ones.

notify.text: A letter from the Civic Court

addr.text: By registered post, to your home address

p.text: attend a hearing on 12 November at 10:00 AM
check the case on the court's official website
No payment is asked of you in this letter.

foot.text: Signed by the Registrar, with the court's stamp

post.label: Arrived by post
post.lens: A registered letter to your home, not a call or a link.
post.why: Courts use official post. A surprise call is a different matter.

subject.label: A case number
subject.lens: A number you can check on the court's official website.
subject.why: You can look it up yourself. A scammer's number cannot be found.

name.label: Your full name
name.lens: Your name and details are right.
name.why: It fits, though a name alone proves little.

attend.label: A hearing date and place
attend.why: Real notices give a date and place you can attend.

check.label: Check on the official site
check.lens: It tells you to check on the court's own website.

nopay.label: Asks for no money
nopay.why: No demand for money fits an honest notice.

sign.label: Signed and stamped
sign.why: Stamps can be copied, so check the case number too.

actions.label: Check the case number on the court's official website I type myself

go_ahead.line: The court's own website listed the case and the hearing. You prepared and went, with no payment asked.

ignore.line: Nothing bad happened this time. But a real court notice must not be ignored: missing a hearing has consequences.

block_report.line: That was a real court notice. A real hearing missed can mean real trouble. Checking, not ignoring, is the skill.
block_report.mirageSays: If you trust nothing, I win anyway.

what_if.block_report: It arrived by post, gave a case number you can check, asked for no money and invited you to a place and date. That is how real notices look.
what_if.ignore: Ignoring was safe. Recognising a real message is the skill: it asks for nothing secret and matches something you know.

golden_rule: A real notice arrives by official post, asks for no money and lets you check the case number yourself. Check, do not ignore.

quick_check.q: What made this court letter genuine?

options.text: It arrived by post, gave a checkable case number and asked for no money

quick_check.explain: Stamps can be copied. A checkable case number and no money are the real signs.

hints.nudge: What is this message actually asking you to do?

rows.v: Check on the court's own website
